reference.title: Band Incline Biceps Curl
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read; the band is anchored low behind the bench so it resists the curl from the bottom)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, short squeeze, about 2.5 s down, brief pause in the stretch

prescription.progression: Band tension is user-chosen: pick one you can curl for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion); add reps, then a stronger band or a rack further back.

cues.text: Set the back pad at about 45-60 degrees with the band looped low round a rack upright behind the bench. Sit back with the hips and upper back on the pad, feet flat, a strand in each hand, arms hanging straight down, palms forward.
Breathe out and curl both hands without letting the elbows swing forward.
Squeeze the biceps where the band is tightest; shoulders stay back on the pad.
Breathe in and lower slowly against the band all the way to straight arms.
Pause briefly in the stretch, arms hanging straight, then repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows swinging forward as the band tightens
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arms hanging; only the forearms move.

mistakes.mistake: Shoulders rolling forward off the pad
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper back on the pad, chest open.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band snap the arms back down
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly, about 2.5 s, then pause at straight arms.
Use 45-60 degrees; raise the pad if the front of the shoulder feels stretched too far (clinical opinion).

kinematics.norm: Full range: mean elbow range was about 117-123 degrees across barbell, EZ-bar and alternating dumbbell curls (Marcolin 2018)

kinematics.measure: Forearm rotation (wrist pron channel, 0 = palm up/forward, 90 = thumb up)
kinematics.norm: Grip changes the biceps/brachioradialis share: the supinated grip gave the highest biceps activity in the lifting phase (Coratella 2023)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm from the trunk line (sagittal)
kinematics.norm: Elbows stay near the sides; a small forward drift at the top is normal, a big swing shifts work to the front deltoid (clinical opinion)

Anchored low behind the bench, the band resists the curl from the first degree and its tension rises as it stretches, so the load is highest near the top; at matched effort elastic tubing and dumbbells gave similar muscle activity (Andersen 2010)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion); biceps activity was lower while lowering than lifting at the same load (Oliveira 2009)
About 45-60 degrees from the floor (common practice, clinical opinion); Oliveira 2009 used an incline bench to put the shoulder in extension

kinematics.measure: Back on the pad (skinned mesh gap)
kinematics.norm: Hips and upper back on the pad, feet flat (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #16968, Band Incline Biceps Curl, video (movement reference)

Kassiano et al. 2025, distinct muscle growth and strength adaptations after preacher and incline biceps curls (Int J Sports Med, randomized trial in 63 young women)

cautions: Elbow or shoulder pain: use a lighter band and shorten the range; stop if pain is sharp (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrists straight (in line with the forearm) (clinical opinion).
Check the band for nicks or tears and loop it securely, low on the upright, so it cannot slide up or slip off.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Front-of-shoulder pain in the stretched position: raise the back pad and use a lighter band (clinical opinion).
modify: Shoulder discomfort: set the pad steeper (60-75 degrees).
Elbow pain: try a neutral (hammer) grip on the incline.
progressions: Stronger band or the rack further back.
Slower lowering with a 1 s pause at the bottom.

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Main elbow flexor; with the arms hanging behind the trunk the long head starts stretched. Incline and standing curls gave similar biceps activation patterns, peaking near 95% of maximum late in the lift (Oliveira 2009), and incline curls grew the proximal elbow flexors more than preacher curls (Kassiano 2025).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Main elbow flexor; with the arms hanging behind the trunk the long head starts stretched. Incline and standing curls gave similar biceps activation patterns, peaking near 95% of maximum late in the lift (Oliveira 2009), and incline curls grew the proximal elbow flexors more than preacher curls (Kassiano 2025).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: Brachioradialis assists; the incline curl showed lower brachioradialis activity than the narrow-grip EZ curl (ACE 2014).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_l: Brachioradialis assists; the incline curl showed lower brachioradialis activity than the narrow-grip EZ curl (ACE 2014).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Wrist and finger flexors grip the band and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Wrist and finger flexors grip the band and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Steadies the shoulder in extension; the incline curl showed less front-deltoid activity than the barbell curl (ACE 2014).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Steadies the shoulder in extension; the incline curl showed less front-deltoid activity than the barbell curl (ACE 2014).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still on the pad.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulder girdle level against the band.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulder girdle level against the band.

phases.label: Back on the pad, arms hanging

guides.label: Hands arc up from behind the trunk line
Elbow bends through a full range
